seriesName: Rex Fleet Academy: Reach and Resolve
format: Academy doctrine/history series told through a recurring seminar cohort, historical case studies, simulations, and occasional field exercises.
storyEngine: Instructor poses a practical doctrine problem; students expose assumptions from different professional and regional backgrounds; a dramatized historical or operational case complicates the easy answer; the class returns to a changed problem rather than a slogan.
canonPrinciples: Reach means restoring contact, trade, rescue capacity, knowledge exchange, and coexistence; it is not synonymous with expansion or Fleet presence.
Resolve means sustaining viable communities, infrastructure, memory, and decision-making when connection fails; it is not synonymous with isolation.
Resolve makes Reach possible; Reach gives Resolve purpose.
The mature problem is balancing both under finite time, capacity, consent, and uncertainty.
Historical sequences must preserve their era: post-Break antecedents may foreshadow later Fleet, Verge, and Shard traditions without importing mature faction design wholesale.

issues.title: The Two Failures
issues.premise: The cohort studies the first rescue vessel after the Resolve Circle and two settlements that nearly fail for opposite reasons: Orison through dependence, Varda through isolation.

issues.title: The Cost of Connection
issues.premise: A reopened corridor brings medicine, standards, credit, and traffic to an independent settlement; the class studies when interoperability becomes dependency or political absorption.

issues.title: The Cost of Standing Alone
issues.premise: A community celebrated for self-sufficiency discovers that its closed technical and civic systems have become brittle; the Academy examines when resilience hardens into refusal to learn.

issues.title: The Verge Rule
issues.premise: A Verge logistics case shows a culture that accepts convoys while building local capacity anyway: take the convoy, build the greenhouse, keep the route open, never assume it will remain open.

issues.title: Who Gets to Decide?
issues.premise: A humanitarian crisis forces the cohort to separate local sovereignty from local coercion and outside assistance from outside jurisdiction.

issues.title: A Ship Is a Contradiction
issues.premise: A training cruise becomes a live operational test: a Fleet ship is a self-sufficient piece of civilization using that independence to reconnect others, forcing the cohort to apply Reach and Resolve without a classroom answer.
